value.tagline: The Eagles go 17-0 and beat the Steelers in Super Bowl CLII for a third straight title, Ryland Maxwell takes the career rushing record, and Bones Crawford throws 64 touchdown passes on his way to a fourth MVP.

articles.headline: Perfect: Eagles Go 17-0, Then Beat the Steelers in Super Bowl CLII
articles.dek: Philadelphia won all 20 of its games, beat Pittsburgh 30-17 at home and gave Dorren Skura a third straight title.
body: Dorren Skura's Eagles did not lose a game in Y93. Philadelphia went 17-0 in the regular season, won three playoff games at home and finished the job with a 30-17 win over the Steelers in Super Bowl CLII, the 152nd edition of the game. It is Skura's third straight title, and no other coach on the board has won more than 6.

The last defeat came in week 5 of Y92, 33-32 at Jacksonville. Every game from there through this Super Bowl was a win, one unbroken run with two championships inside it. It was Skura's first unbeaten regular season since the Falcons of Y87.

Nobody else played to that standard. The Eagles allowed 363 points, the fewest in the league, scored 622, second only to Houston's 640, and finished first in the power rankings with a point differential of 259. They were 8-0 at home, 9-0 on the road, 8-0 against clubs with winning records and 5-0 in one-score games.

The perfect season nearly ended on the last day of the regular season, a 24-23 escape at the Giants. In the playoffs the Vikings fell 40-34 in the divisional round and New York lost again, 38-28, in the conference final. Pittsburgh arrived from the wild-card round, playing its 21st game of the season, and lost to Philadelphia for the third time in three meetings on file.

Ryland Maxwell, "Mad Max", was named Super Bowl MVP for the 5th time and collected his 10th ring. Bones Crawford was the league's Most Valuable Player after throwing 64 touchdown passes, and Keenan Viennes was Offensive Player of the Year with 2,007 receiving yards.

articles.headline: Mad Max Passes McCoy and Takes the Career Rushing Record
articles.dek: Ryland Maxwell ran for 2,145 yards in Y93 and finished at 25,701, 1,194 clear of Lane McCoy. He also took the club's career rushing touchdowns mark.
body: A year ago Ryland Maxwell sat 951 yards behind Lane McCoy on the career rushing list. McCoy did not play in Y93, and Maxwell did not slow down. He ran for 2,145 yards and 26 touchdowns in all 20 of Philadelphia's games, caught 23 passes for 10 more scores, and finished the season with 25,701 career rushing yards, the most on file and 1,194 ahead of McCoy.

The record board kept by Skura's clubs now lists him for both career rushing marks: 25,701 yards and 355 touchdowns. The second is a club record only. Across the whole league McCoy's 458 rushing touchdowns still stand first.

The market moved with him again. His Career Legacy rose from 11,001 to 11,965, past Rondale Ikarras at 11,725, so no running back on file now rates higher. His card's value climbed from 29,409 to 33,647. He has 10 rings, every one of them won with Skura across three clubs, and he has 5 Super Bowl MVPs.

articles.headline: The Doctor Throws 64 Touchdown Passes and Wins a Fourth MVP
articles.dek: Bones Crawford played all 20 games, threw for 4,936 yards and won his fifth ring, every one of them in Philadelphia.
body: A year after injury cost him 4 games, Bones Crawford, "The Doctor", was on the field for all 20 of Philadelphia's games. He threw for 4,936 yards and 64 touchdowns with 11 interceptions, 3.2 touchdown passes a game.

The league named him Most Valuable Player for the 4th time. Nobody threw more touchdown passes; Tim Sweeney of the Texans was next with 45. Crawford's overall rose from 80 to 86, his Career Legacy from 7,332 to 8,158, and his card's value by 142.6%.

He has 5 rings, all won with the Eagles. He had help: tight end Jacob Proise caught 46 passes for 837 yards, and Akiem Brock made 51 blocks, more than any other lineman in the league, as his overall climbed to 94.

articles.headline: Viennes Catches for 2,007 Yards and Is Offensive Player of the Year
articles.dek: Keenan Viennes caught 107 passes for 2,007 yards and 29 touchdowns in his second season. Calvin Wingo II finished 31 yards behind him.
body: A year ago Keenan Viennes stepped into Kaulani Rahman's place as a rookie. In his second season nobody in the league caught for more. Viennes played all 20 games and caught 107 passes for 2,007 yards and 29 touchdowns, 18.8 yards a catch, and was named Offensive Player of the Year.

The closest pursuer wore the same uniform. Calvin Wingo II, last season's winner, caught 104 passes for 1,976 yards and 19 touchdowns, and no other receiver in the league reached even half of that yardage. Wingo's overall rose from 83 to 86. Viennes's rose from 68 to 73, and his card's value jumped 226.7%, the biggest gain on the market.
Two seasons in, Viennes has 2 rings, 3,763 career receiving yards and 48 touchdown catches in 40 games.

articles.headline: Watts Is Defensive Player of the Year, and Lazard Is the Rookie of the Year
articles.dek: DQ Watts made 225 tackles and 5 interceptions for 13-4 Houston. Alshon Lazard threw 39 touchdown passes for 14-3 Cincinnati.
body: DQ Watts, a Defensive Rookie of the Year earlier in his career, added the bigger award in Y93. The Texans defensive back made 225 tackles and intercepted 5 passes in 19 games, and his overall rose from 75 to 78. Houston went 13-4, scored 640 points, the most in the league, and got 45 touchdown passes from Tim Sweeney against 4 interceptions.

The Offensive Rookie of the Year played in Cincinnati. Alshon Lazard threw for 3,561 yards and 39 touchdowns with 4 interceptions in 18 games and ran for 10 more scores. The Bengals went 14-3 and finished second in the power rankings.
Neither club reached the Super Bowl. The Texans were out after two playoff games, the Bengals after one, and the Raiders, also 14-3, went out in their first game as well.

articles.headline: Three Tries, Three Losses: Ty Lock's Giants Still Cannot Beat Philadelphia
articles.dek: New York lost 30-22, 24-23 and 38-28 to the Eagles and had not beaten Philadelphia in any meeting since Y88. Washington was swept again.
body: Ty Lock won two rings with Skura's Jets, in Y80 and Y82, with Ryland Maxwell in the same backfield. A trade sent him to the Giants before Y83, and he has been on the other side ever since. In Y93 he faced his old coach three times.

New York lost 30-22 in Philadelphia in week 15. In week 18 the Giants came within a point at home, losing 24-23, the narrowest of the Eagles' 20 wins. They met again in the conference final and lost 38-28. Lock threw for 3,550 yards and 26 touchdowns with 3 interceptions, and Niles Canaday ran for 1,898 yards and 40 touchdowns, the most in the league. Since Y88 the Giants had not beaten the Eagles once.
The Commanders, who had split the series for three straight seasons before Y92, were swept for the second year running, 48-22 in Philadelphia and 40-28 in Washington.

articles.headline: A Year On, Dwayne Skura and Kaulani Rahman Watch the Eagles Win Again
articles.dek: The two champions Philadelphia traded before Y92 had solid seasons in Indianapolis and Los Angeles. Both clubs went out after one playoff game.
body: Dwayne Skura, last season's Defensive Player of the Year, made 216 tackles and 2 interceptions in 18 games for the Colts. Indianapolis went 11-6, finished fifth in the power rankings and lost its only playoff game. Skura saw his overall rise from 81 to 84.
Kaulani Rahman caught 71 passes for 620 yards and 5 touchdowns in 18 games for the Rams, who improved to 10-7 and were also one and done in the playoffs. His overall rose from 89 to 90.

Philadelphia did not miss either of them. Koa Zuber, "Uber Feasts", intercepted 6 passes, more than any other defender in the league. Keesean Hand added 121 tackles and 3 interceptions in the secondary, and Viennes, Rahman's replacement, and Calvin Wingo II finished first and second in the league in receiving yards.

articles.headline: Hainsey Closes In on Two Career Records, and Bello Is a Sack From Suh
articles.dek: Odell Hainsey is 2 interceptions behind Damar Hobbs and 196 tackles behind K'Lavon Settle. Deshone Bello needs 1 sack to tie Kalif Suh.
body: Damar Hobbs took the career interceptions record a year ago and did not play in Y93. His 43 now have company in the rear-view mirror. Odell Hainsey of the Chargers intercepted 4 passes and made 183 tackles in 17 games, and he has 41 interceptions and 2,989 tackles for his career: 2 short of Hobbs and 196 short of K'Lavon Settle's career tackles record of 3,185. His overall rose from 94 to 97.
Deshone Bello of the Jets had 3 sacks, tied for the most in the league, and has 23 for his career, 1 behind Kalif Suh's league record of 24.

Further down the lists, Siran Spector of the Texans ran for 24 touchdowns and has 373, 1 behind Rondale Ikarras for fifth on the career list. Kyron Atwell made 199 tackles for the Jets and now has 2,853. Lane McCoy, who did not play this season either, still holds the career rushing touchdowns record at 458.

articles.headline: Quick Hits
body: Jakeem Friend, a Seahawks lineman for most of his career, entered the Hall of Fame as the Class of Y93 with 7 rings and 557 blocks.
Josh Brooks of the Commanders threw 43 touchdown passes in 19 games without an interception.
Tevin Fox of the Panthers played his 400th game and has 69,973 passing yards and 618 touchdown passes without a ring.
The 4-13 Titans won 31-30 at Pittsburgh in week 4, the upset of the season, against the club that would reach the Super Bowl.
The Packers beat the Cardinals 65-13 in week 15, and the Broncos outlasted the Chargers 58-51 in week 17, 109 points in all.
The Jets tied twice, 24-24 with the Broncos and 26-26 with the Patriots, and finished 5-10-2.
The Cardinals allowed 680 points, the most in the league, and the Saints went 0-9 on the road.

value.tagline: The Eagles repeat with Super Bowl CLI over Dwayne Skura's Colts, Lane McCoy and Ryland Maxwell both pass Rondale Ikarras, and Kyron Atwell enters the Hall of Fame.

articles.headline: Back to Back: Eagles Beat the Colts in Super Bowl CLI
articles.dek: Philadelphia went 15-2, won every game after week 5 and beat Indianapolis 30-21 on the Colts' own field for Dorren Skura's second title in a row.
body: Dorren Skura's Eagles are champions again. Philadelphia beat the Colts 30-21 in Super Bowl CLI, the 151st edition of the game, played in Indianapolis, and kept the trophy it took back from Houston a year ago. Skura's lead on the coaches' title board grew again; no other coach on it has more than 6.

It did not start that way. The Eagles lost two of their first five games, both on the road and both by three points or fewer: 35-32 at Chicago and 33-32 at Jacksonville. Then the losing stopped. Philadelphia won every game after that, 12 in the regular season and 3 more in the playoffs, and the run was still alive when the season ended.

Over the full season nobody was close. The Eagles scored 652 points, the most in the league, allowed 373, the fewest, and finished first in the power rankings with a point differential of 279. They went 9-0 at home, a year after going 9-0 on the road.

The playoffs asked more of the offense than a year ago. Green Bay scored 36 in the divisional round and lost 44-36. Seattle scored 34 in the conference final and lost 46-34. In the Super Bowl the Eagles met a Colts team they had beaten 40-10 in week 14, and they won again.

Ryland Maxwell, "Mad Max", was named Super Bowl MVP at the end of a season in which he ran for 2,839 yards. Calvin Wingo II was Offensive Player of the Year. On the other sideline stood Dwayne Skura, a champion in Philadelphia a year earlier, traded to Indianapolis before the season and named Defensive Player of the Year. He had to watch his old team lift the trophy again.

articles.headline: Lane McCoy Passes Ikarras, and Maxwell Follows Him
articles.dek: McCoy ended Y92 holding the career rushing record at 24,507 yards. Ryland Maxwell ran past Rondale Ikarras's 23,178 in the same season and finished it 951 yards behind.
body: Rondale Ikarras's career rushing record fell early in Y92, and by the end of the season it had been passed twice. Lane McCoy of the Broncos began the year 90 yards behind Ikarras, "The Prodigal Son", and ran for 1,419 yards and 29 touchdowns in 19 games. He finishes with 24,507 career yards, 1,329 clear of the old mark of 23,178, and his touchdown record now stands at 458. In 326 games he still has no ring.

The second back past Ikarras came from Philadelphia. Ryland Maxwell ran for 2,839 yards, the most in any season on file, and closed the year at 23,556, 378 beyond Ikarras and 951 behind McCoy. A year ago that gap would have looked permanent. After this season it looks like a race.
Denver had a good year around its record holder. The Broncos went 11-6 with a rookie quarterback, Sione Garland, and McCoy gave him the ground game to lean on.

articles.headline: Mad Max Runs for 2,839 Yards and Takes a Fourth Super Bowl MVP
articles.dek: Ryland Maxwell played all 20 games, ran for 32 touchdowns and won his ninth ring, every one of them with Dorren Skura.
body: A year after coming home to Skura, Ryland Maxwell had the biggest season a running back has had on file. He played all 20 of Philadelphia's games and ran for 2,839 yards and 32 touchdowns, 142 yards a game, and he caught 22 passes for 11 more scores.

He saved the last word for the last game. Maxwell was named MVP of Super Bowl CLI, the fourth Super Bowl MVP of his career, and the win gave him 9 rings, all won with Skura: two with the Jets, five with the Falcons and two with the Eagles.

The market moved with him. His card's value rose 131.2%, from 12,722 to 29,409, his Career Legacy climbed from 9,794 to 11,001 and his grade went from A plus to S. Among running backs only Rondale Ikarras, at 11,914, has a higher Career Legacy, and Maxwell is now ahead of Ikarras in career rushing yards.

articles.headline: Rahman to the Rams, Skura to the Colts, and a Reunion in the Super Bowl
articles.dek: Philadelphia traded two of its champions before the season. Dwayne Skura was named Defensive Player of the Year and met his old team for the title.
body: The Eagles broke up part of their core before Y92. Receiver Kaulani Rahman, who caught 102 passes for 1,893 yards a year ago, was traded to the Rams. Defensive back Dwayne Skura, who won rings in Philadelphia in Y88, Y89 and Y91, was traded to the Colts.

Skura made Indianapolis look smart. He played all 21 of the Colts' games, made 233 tackles, the most in the league, intercepted 5 passes and was named Defensive Player of the Year for the first time. The Colts went 11-6, won the AFC South and reached Super Bowl CLI, where the opponent was Philadelphia. The Eagles had beaten them 40-10 in week 14 and beat them again, 30-21. Skura finished on the wrong side of the team he had won with.

Rahman's first season in Los Angeles was quieter: 57 catches, 637 yards and 9 touchdowns in 18 games for a Rams team that went 9-8 and lost 48-15 in Philadelphia in week 4. His grade slipped from S to A plus. The Eagles barely felt the loss, because the rookie Keenan Viennes caught 91 passes for 1,756 yards in Rahman's old place.

articles.headline: Viennes and Hand Win Rings as Rookies, and Garland Throws 40 in Denver
articles.dek: Keenan Viennes caught 1,756 yards for the champions. Sione Garland threw 40 touchdown passes and 1 interception for the Broncos.
body: Philadelphia's two newcomers stepped straight into a champion's lineup. Keenan Viennes caught 91 passes for 1,756 yards and 19 touchdowns in all 20 games, 19.3 yards a catch, and his card opens with an S grade. Defensive back Keesean Hand made 135 tackles, 2 interceptions and 2 forced fumbles in 17 games; he missed 3 through injury. Both end their first season with a ring.

The best rookie quarterback played in Denver. Sione Garland threw for 3,351 yards and 40 touchdowns with 1 interception in 19 games for the 11-6 Broncos. In Tampa Bay, Ja'Marr Chark threw 25 touchdown passes for a club that finished 5-11-1.

The awards went elsewhere. Teven Charles of the 12-5 Panthers was Offensive Rookie of the Year with 62 catches, 552 yards and 8 touchdowns, and Colts defensive lineman Amik Barnes was Defensive Rookie of the Year with 114 tackles. Cardinals running back Roderic Trawick ran for 1,455 yards and 29 touchdowns in 17 games without catching a pass.

articles.headline: Wingo Is Offensive Player of the Year, and Crawford Throws 49 in 16 Games
articles.dek: Calvin Wingo II caught 22 touchdowns in his third season. Bones Crawford missed 4 games through injury and still threw as many touchdown passes as anyone.
body: Calvin Wingo II keeps filling the shelf. Offensive Rookie of the Year in Y90 and Super Bowl MVP in Y91, the receiver caught 98 passes for 1,764 yards and 22 touchdowns in 20 games and was named Offensive Player of the Year. His overall rose from 75 to 83. Through 60 career games he has 355 catches, 6,552 yards and 68 touchdowns.

Bones Crawford, "The Doctor", played 16 of the Eagles' 20 games and missed 4 through injury. In the 16 he threw for 3,556 yards and 49 touchdowns, the same total Korey Friend of the Colts reached in 21 games, and nobody threw more. The cost was 17 interceptions. His Career Legacy climbed from 6,826 to 7,332 and his card's value from 344 to 1,047.
Tight end Jacob Proise added 12 touchdown catches, and the Eagles finished with the most points in the league.

articles.headline: Atwell Enters the Hall, McQuay Returns and Hobbs Takes the Interceptions Record
articles.dek: Kyron Atwell crossed the 7,500 bar. Kyric McQuay climbed back over it, Keion Orzech is back above the floor and Damar Hobbs now has 43 career interceptions.
body: The Y92 class is one man. Kyron Atwell of the Jets made 230 tackles and 4 interceptions in 17 games, and his Career Legacy rose from 7,137 to 7,780. He has 2,654 career tackles, 39 interceptions and a Defensive Player of the Year award, and he is still playing.

Two familiar names are back. Kyric McQuay, "Baby Manning", a two-time champion with the Colts who had been removed from the Hall, saw his Career Legacy move from 7,459 to 7,531, past the 7,500 bar, the only way back in. Keion Orzech, who dropped out a year ago, rose from 7,283 to 7,364, back above the 7,300 floor that inducted members must hold. Terron Stidham, inducted last year, slipped from 7,522 to 7,473 and stays in.

Atwell's next target is a record. Damar Hobbs of the Patriots intercepted 4 passes and went past Daren Teamer's 42 to take the career mark at 43, while making 229 tackles for a club that went 2-15. Atwell is 4 behind him.

articles.headline: Chicago Again, Jacksonville by a Point, and a Sweep of Washington
articles.dek: The Eagles lost only twice, 35-32 at Chicago and 33-32 at Jacksonville. They swept the Commanders and still had not lost to the Giants since Y88.
body: For the second year running the Bears beat Philadelphia when almost nobody else could. Chicago finished 5-11-1 and 25th in the power rankings, and in week 3 it won 35-32, the upset of the year for the second straight season. That left the series since Y88 level.
Two weeks later Jacksonville won 33-32, a one-point game on the road. The Jaguars finished 8-9. It was the narrowest defeat of the Eagles' season.

The Commanders, who had split the series three seasons in a row, got no split this time. Philadelphia won 32-16 at home in the opener and 38-26 in Washington in week 8, its first sweep of Washington since Y88. The Giants came closest to an upset of their own: they lost 38-37 in Philadelphia in week 9 and 40-22 at home in the final week. Skura's Eagles closed the year without a loss to New York in any meeting since Y88.

articles.headline: Suh, Heath, Peters and Eleven More Retire
articles.dek: Fourteen veterans walked away before Y92, among them the Jets linebacker Kalif Suh and the quarterbacks Kahzin Heath and Pete Peters. Andrew Dwight and Russ Bello are free agents.
body: Kalif Suh spent his career with the Jets, won 3 rings there, the last in Y82, and leaves with 980 tackles, 24 sacks, 17 interceptions and 10 forced fumbles. He is a Hall of Famer with a Career Legacy of 9,048.

Kahzin Heath of the Broncos, an Offensive Rookie of the Year and an MVP, retires with 60,046 passing yards and 572 touchdown passes in 344 games. Pete Peters of the Buccaneers leaves with 60,169 yards and 557 touchdowns in 337 games.

Quenton Fuller, a Hall of Famer since last year, leaves the Chargers' defensive line with 1,355 tackles. Keelan Blair ran for 17,346 yards and 313 touchdowns for the Cardinals. Five tight ends go at once: Fred Kmet, Dare Talib, Gus Langley, Damarri Melvin and Derek Amadi. So do Yasir Gray, Cordell Bulaga, Thomas Gano and Mykal Mosby.
Andrew Dwight, the Colts' Defensive Player of the Year in Y91, and Rams receiver Russ Bello are free agents.

articles.headline: Quick Hits
body: The Colts beat the Ravens 69-12 in week 1, the biggest margin and the most points by one club in the weekly scores on file.
Korey Friend of the Colts was MVP after throwing for 4,724 yards and 49 touchdowns with 4 interceptions in 21 games.
Akiem Brock made 63 blocks for the Eagles, 21 more than any other lineman, and his overall rose from 86 to 91.
Quincy Booker intercepted 6 passes for Philadelphia, no defender had more, and his grade rose from B to A.
Snoop Dotson had 4 sacks, tied for the most in the league, and won his third ring.
The Panthers beat the Vikings 64-36 in week 13, 100 points, the shootout of the year.
Alton Yeldon of the Seahawks ran for 39 touchdowns, the most in the league, and Buffalo went 13-4 to finish second in the power rankings.

value.intro: Y93 gave Philadelphia a perfect season and Ryland Maxwell the rushing record. Perfection hides things, and records flatter. The arguments below are ours to defend; every figure comes straight from the league data.

takes.headline: Perfect Is Not the Same as Dominant: The 17-0 Eagles Were the League's Luckiest Club
takes.dek: Philadelphia's points say 13.3 wins. The schedule was soft and every close game broke its way.
body: Nobody gets to take 17-0 away from Philadelphia, and nobody should pretend the record tells the whole story either. By points scored and allowed, the Eagles played like a 13.3-win team. They won 3.7 games more than that, the biggest gap between expectation and result of any club in the league. They went 4-0 in one-score games. Their schedule rated 0.455; only the Raiders and Panthers drew softer slates.

Here is the uncomfortable part. The Y92 Eagles, the team that lost twice, outscored opponents by 279. This one managed 259. The perfect team was not the best team Dorren Skura has had in Philadelphia. It was the one the bounces loved, and the next one will not get all of them.

takes.headline: Bones Crawford Is Already a Better Quarterback Than Ty Lock Ever Was
takes.dek: Four MVPs in 113 games against two in 295. The argument is over.
body: Ty Lock has the reputation, the ratings and the longer career. Bones Crawford has everything else. The Doctor won his 4th MVP in Y93 after throwing 64 touchdown passes and 4,936 yards in 20 games. Lock, also in 20 games, threw 26 touchdowns for the Giants.

This is not one season. Crawford has averaged 3.31 touchdown passes a game across 113 career games. Lock has averaged 1.95 across 295, and has 2 MVPs to show for it. He threw only 11 interceptions all year. Longevity is a virtue, and Lock has it. Greatness is a different thing, and Crawford has more of it already.

takes.headline: Ty Lock's Card Rose 30% in a Down Season. The Market Is Paying for a Name.
takes.dek: His touchdowns fell from 32 to 26 and his price jumped to 4,458. A rookie with 39 sells for 16.
body: Ty Lock threw 26 touchdown passes in Y93, down from 32 a year earlier, and his card went up 30% anyway, to 4,458. That is more than double Bones Crawford's 2,198, and Crawford just threw 64. The market still reads an overall of 92 for Lock, and it is pricing that rating, not the production.

Meanwhile Alshon Lazard threw 39 touchdowns with 4 interceptions as a rookie in Cincinnati, and his card sits at 16. Lock has earned his place in the league's history. Paying a premium for what he did in Y93 is buying a memory. The smart money sells the name and buys the rookie.

takes.headline: Josh Brooks Threw 43 Touchdown Passes and Not One Interception, and the League Barely Noticed
takes.dek: The cleanest season in the league belonged to a quarterback with 558 career touchdowns and no rings.
body: Bones Crawford's 64 touchdowns will get the headlines, and fine. But the most remarkable quarterback season of Y93 happened in Washington. Josh Brooks played 19 games, threw for 4,061 yards and 43 touchdowns, and not one of his passes was intercepted.

Brooks now has 558 career touchdown passes and 0 rings. He has spent the last six seasons in the same division as Skura's Eagles, and a 10-7 Commanders club finished third in its own division behind the Eagles and Giants. The league hands out rings to teams. If it handed out a trophy for quarterbacking without mistakes, Brooks would have won it this year by a mile.

takes.headline: Niles Canaday Scored 40 Touchdowns and Caught 3 Passes. That Is Not a Star.
takes.dek: The Giants back outscored Ryland Maxwell on the ground and gave his offense nothing else.
body: Niles Canaday ran for 1,898 yards and 40 touchdowns in Y93, 14 more rushing scores than Ryland Maxwell. Somebody will call him the next great back. Look closer. Canaday caught 3 passes all season for 54 yards. Maxwell caught 23 and scored 10 more touchdowns through the air.

The market is not fooled either: it reads an overall of 69 and prices his card at 22. Touchdowns say as much about where a back gets the ball as about the back. A back who only runs is a highlight reel with one page, and the first defense that takes his carries away will expose it.

takes.headline: The Best Defender in Y93 Played for the 3-14 Saints, and His Card Costs 614
takes.dek: Trequan Roberts made 241 tackles in 17 games. The Defensive Player of the Year made 225 in 19.
body: DQ Watts won Defensive Player of the Year for Houston, and the award formula, which leans hard on interceptions, explains why: Watts picked off 5 passes to Trequan Roberts' 1. That is the whole case. Roberts made 241 tackles in 17 games, 14.2 a game. Watts made 225 in 19, 11.8 a game.

Roberts did it for a Saints team that went 3-14, and the market treats him accordingly at 614. Odell Hainsey's card sells for 7,788 after a season of 183 tackles in 17 games. One of these defenders carried a collapsing team every week. The other carries a reputation. Only one of them is priced like a star.

takes.headline: Keenan Viennes Is the Offensive Player of the Year and His Card Still Costs 49
takes.dek: He out-gained and out-scored Calvin Wingo II, whose card sells for 667. The market is a season behind.
body: Keenan Viennes caught 107 passes for 2,007 yards and 29 touchdowns and won Offensive Player of the Year. His own teammate Calvin Wingo II caught 104 for 1,976 and 19. Viennes beat him in every column that matters. Wingo's card is 667. Viennes' card is 49.

The gap is a ratings story. The market reads an overall of 73 for Viennes against 86 for Wingo, and Viennes has only 40 career games behind him. The market already grades his skill an S, the top mark on its scale. Buy him now. In two seasons nobody will believe he was ever this cheap.

takes.headline: Alshon Lazard Is Already a Top Five Quarterback, and the Ratings Have Not Caught Up
takes.dek: Only three passers threw more touchdowns than the Rookie of the Year. His overall says otherwise.
body: Alshon Lazard threw 39 touchdown passes and 4 interceptions in 18 games for a Bengals club that went 14-3, and he won Rookie of the Year. Only Bones Crawford, Tim Sweeney and Josh Brooks threw more touchdowns. Juju Ngakoue matched him at 39 with 267 career games behind him.

The ratings have not noticed. The market reads an overall of 63 for Lazard and sells his card for 16. He is producing like a veteran on a rating that has nowhere to go but up. Cincinnati has its quarterback for the next decade, and the rest of the conference should be worried.

takes.headline: Ryland Maxwell Took the Career Rushing Record in the Season His Decline Began
takes.dek: He ran for 694 fewer yards than in Y92. He will finish third on the all-time Career Legacy list, not first.
body: Ryland Maxwell owns the career rushing record at 25,701 yards and won his 5th Super Bowl MVP. Celebrate it. Then look at the line. Mad Max ran for 2,145 yards in 20 games, 694 fewer than his record 2,839 in Y92. That is 107 yards a game, down from 142. His rushing touchdowns fell from 32 to 26.

His Career Legacy of 11,965 ranks third all time, 590 behind God Johnson and 1,426 behind Sherman Brandson. He gained 964 this season. One more year like this catches Johnson. Brandson is out of reach, and the greatest-ever debate ends with a running back in third place.

takes.headline: The Raiders' 14-3 Was the Emptiest Record in Football
takes.dek: Las Vegas played the softest schedule in the league and still won about three games more than its points earned.
body: The Raiders and Bengals both finished 14-3, and only one of them earned it. Cincinnati's opponents rated 0.502, an average slate. Las Vegas drew a 0.427 schedule, the softest of all 32 clubs. By points scored and allowed the Raiders were an 11.2-win team, and they beat that by 2.8 games, a margin only the Eagles topped.

Houston went 13-4 and outscored opponents by 198, far more than the Raiders' 145. That is the AFC's best team by the numbers. When the Raiders meet a schedule with teeth, the record will look like what it was: good, lucky and soft.

takes.headline: Pittsburgh Reached the Super Bowl Without Winning Its Own Division
takes.dek: The Steelers finished behind Cincinnati, lost to a 4-13 Titans team and ranked No. 7 in power.
body: The Steelers went 11-6, finished second in the AFC North behind the Bengals, and lost 31-30 at home to a Titans team that won 4 games all year. They outscored opponents by 38 across the regular season. The power table ranked them No. 7, behind four AFC clubs.

Then they won when it counted, and credit to them for that. But Super Bowl CLII was never really a contest of equals. Philadelphia won 30-17 against a club whose points said 9.3 wins. The AFC sent the team that got hot, not its best one.
